answer: The declaration is a zenith header, so 1809 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in grove, thus the distribution is public, and quartz lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. A farm of 93 pays that 197 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
